title: Neil Ian Uy
text: Neil Ian Uy, MSc IT, is the Dean of the Information and Computer Technologies Faculty. He graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Information Technology from Negros Oriental State University in Dumaguete City, Philippines, and completed his Master’s Degree in Information Technology at the same university, specializing in Systems Analysis and Design. With more than 17 years of experience in IT Professional Services, his areas of expertise include Requirements Engineering, Applied Software Design and Architecture, Project Management with Agile Scrum and ITIL, and Computer Systems Servicing Level 2. He holds a Mile 2 Cybersecurity C)PEH certificate and advocates cybersecurity awareness, personal data protection, and privacy. He also volunteers with NGOs by providing technical support, basic computer literacy training, and competency development. In addition, he provides free online tutorial courses to students in less privileged areas of the Philippines who are interested in learning about Information Technology.

title: Sreyteav Sry
text: Sreyteav Sry, MSc MIS, is the Head of the Management of Information Systems Department at Paragon International University. Born and raised in Takeo province, Cambodia, she earned a Bachelor of Science in Management of Information Systems from Paragon International University in 2020. During her bachelor’s studies, she worked as a part-time web developer at a startup company and as a teaching assistant for MIS 112 – IT Applications for Business and MIS 110 – Introduction to IT Applications. She later worked full-time as an IT officer at a microfinance institute in Phnom Penh. In 2021, she joined the STAR program at Paragon International University, where she pursued a Master of Science in Management of Information Systems and worked as a teaching and administrative assistant in the ICT faculty. She earned her MSc in Management of Information Systems from Paragon International University in 2022. Currently, she is a full-time lecturer and Head of the Management of Information Systems Department. Her research interests include Khmer natural language processing, deep learning, and data science. Her publication includes: Sry, S., & Nguyen, A. S. (2022). A review of Khmer word segmentation and part-of-speech tagging and an experimental study using bidirectional long short-term memory. HO CHI MINH CITY OPEN UNIVERSITY JOURNAL OF SCIENCE-ENGINEERING AND TECHNOLOGY, 12(1), 23-34.

title: Flordeliza P. Poncio
text: Flordeliza P. Poncio, MSc IT, is the Head of the Computer Science Department. She graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science from the University of the Cordilleras, Baguio City, Philippines, in 2011. She completed her Master’s Degree in Information Technology, majoring in Enterprise Systems, at the same university in 2013 through the Faculty Development Program, a scholarship granted by the Commission on Higher Education. She is also a Licensed Professional Teacher with a major in Mathematics. Her research interests include eLearning, eCommerce, Data Mining, Text Analysis and Mining, and Business Intelligence. She is a faculty member of the Department of Information and Communication Technologies at Paragon International University, Cambodia. Her publication includes Configuration and Implementation of the SAP ERP ECC 6.0 Sales and Distribution Module for the University of the Cordilleras.

title: Ratana Soth
text: Ratana Soth, MSc ITE, is a Lecturer in the Faculty of ICT, Manager of the ParagonIU Cloud Server Lab, and Director of the Applied Research and Development Initiative Center (RaDiCe). He is an IT professional with over 18 years of experience in software development and systems administration, including cloud infrastructure, Windows and Linux servers, web technologies, web security, and various software frameworks. As a lecturer at Paragon International University, he teaches technological concepts and integrates cloud technologies into research and learning environments through his role as Cloud Server Lab Manager. As Director of RaDiCe, he leads applied research projects. His professional experience includes serving as National IT Consultant for the Ministry of Commerce, IT Consultant at HBS Law, Chief Technical Officer at Mekong Market Co., Ltd., and Chief Information Officer at BNG Legal before joining ParagonIU. He earned a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science from Norton University, Cambodia, in 2007 and a Master of Science in Information Technology Engineering from the Royal University of Phnom Penh, Cambodia, in 2023. He is currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Information Technology at Lincoln University College, Malaysia.

title: Ruslan Isaev
text: Ruslan Isaev, Ph.D., is the Associate Dean of the Information and Computer Technologies Faculty at Paragon International University, Phnom Penh, Cambodia. He previously served as Dean of the Faculty of Engineering and Informatics at Ala-Too International University in Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic. He earned a Specialist Degree in Programming and Computational Mathematics from Bashkir State Pedagogical University named after M. Akmulla, Ufa, Russia, from 2001 to 2006, and completed doctoral studies in Theoretical Physics with a focus on Astrophysics and Dark Matter from 2009 to 2012. His research interests include artificial intelligence, virtual reality, robotics, UAV systems, natural language processing, cybersecurity, and ethical hacking through CTF competitions. His featured publications include HIVA: Holographic Intellectual Voice Assistant, presented at ICECCO 2023; Design and Implementation of Wall-Scale Vector Art Drawing Robot, published in the ACM International Conference Proceeding Series in 2024; and Classification of Tents in Street Bazaars Using CNN, presented at CompSysTech 2025. He also participates in sport and cybersport and competitive challenges involving strategic and analytical skills.

title: Haksrun Lao
text: Haksrun Lao, MSc MIS, is an Academic Affairs Coordinator, educator, researcher, and technology professional based in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, with expertise in computer science, information systems, and multilingual education. He is currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Computer Science at Paragon International University, where he serves as Academic Affairs Coordinator in the Office of Academic Affairs and lectures in the Faculty of Information and Computer Technologies. His teaching portfolio includes Object-Oriented Programming, Operating Systems, and Software Testing and Quality Assurance. Fluent in Khmer, Chinese, and English, he has experience in academic practice, software product management, and cross-cultural communication, supported by academic distinctions and professional certifications. He earned an MSc in Management Information Systems from Paragon International University, Cambodia, in 2024 and a BSc in Computer Science and Technology from Hangzhou Dianzi University, China, in 2020. His publications include STICformer: spatio-temporal intrinsic connections transformer for traffic flow prediction; RGB-D camera and graph neural network-based SLAM for dynamic and low-texture environments; Trustworthy and efficient project scheduling in IIoT based on smart contracts and edge computing; Traffic Safety Oriented Multi-Intersection Flow Prediction Based on Transformer and CNN; Distributed reinforcement learning-based memory allocation for edge-PLCs in industrial IoT; and A Time-Overlapping Multiplex VLC System for End-Edge Data Transmission.

title: Vichera Heang
text: Vichera HEANG, M.Arch, is the Dean of the Engineering Faculty and a member of the Academic and Executive Boards at Paragon International University. She holds a Master’s degree in Architecture from Gazi University, Turkey, and undergraduate degrees in Interior Architecture and English Language from Cambodia. She also serves as a board member of the Architects Association Khmer (AAK). Throughout her academic journey, she participated in exchange programs across several Asian countries and gained professional experience as an interior designer and architect on projects in Cambodia. She later transitioned into academia as an architecture lecturer at universities in Phnom Penh and served as Head of the Architecture Department before becoming Dean of the Engineering Faculty. Her research focuses on sustainability and traditional Cambodian houses, particularly integrating traditional elements into contemporary design while preserving Cambodian cultural heritage. Education: M.A. in Architecture, Gazi University, Ankara, Turkey, 2018; B.A. in Interior Architecture, Limkokwing University of Creative Technology, Phnom Penh, Cambodia, 2013; B.A. in English Language, University of Puthisastra, Phnom Penh, Cambodia, 2013.

title: MengLeang Lay
text: MengLeang LAY, Ph.D, is a Career Advisor, faculty member, and board member at Paragon International University. Before joining ParagonU, he worked with the Impact Engineering research group on research funded by the Australian Research Council in collaboration with The University of Melbourne and Swinburne University of Technology. The project involved large-scale impact experiments on full-scale reinforced concrete walls to develop practical structural design solutions for barriers. He was also involved with the startup MEDIKEY, where his team adapted technology to assist the FinTech industry in combating money laundering. At ParagonU, he has been involved in teaching, academic advising, and the Higher Education Improvement Project funded by the World Bank and the Royal Government of Cambodia to improve STEM teaching quality. His team has also worked on international partnerships, exchange programs, and a 2+2 program for engineering students. Education: Ph.D. in Construction Management, Universiti Teknologi Malaysia, Malaysia, expected 2024; Master of Engineering (Structural), The University of Melbourne, Australia, 2019; BSc in Civil Engineering, Zaman University, Phnom Penh, Cambodia, 2017. His publication includes Key factors affecting construction safety performance in developing countries: Evidence from Cambodia, Construction Economics and Building, 17(4), 48.

title: Pahlaj Moolio
text: Pahlaj MOOLIO, Ph.D, is the Dean of the Economics and Administrative Sciences Faculty and Dean of the Mathematics and Sciences Faculty at Paragon International University. He is a mathematician, statistician, and econometrician with an international academic and research career. He pursued higher education in Pakistan and Bangladesh, developing expertise in mathematics, statistics, mathematical economics, and econometrics. His professional experience spans Pakistan, Bangladesh, Thailand, Germany, the United States, and Cambodia. In Thailand, he served as a member of the Board of Directors of Santitham Education and Development Foundation. In Germany, he served as a DAAD Guest Professor, and in the United States he serves as a Research Fellow of Yale University’s Global Justice Program. Since 2002, he has been based in Cambodia, teaching mathematics, statistics, and econometrics and participating in research and academic development. He has also provided consultancy services to Cambodian governmental institutions and international non-governmental organizations on development projects funded by organizations including ADB, the World Bank, EU, JICA, KOIKA, and SIDA. Education: Ph.D. in Mathematical Economics, University of Chittagong, Bangladesh; M.Phil. in Mathematical Economics, University of Chittagong, Bangladesh; M.Sc. in Mathematics, University of Sindh, Pakistan; B.Sc. (Hons.) in Mathematics with Statistics as a minor, University of Sindh, Pakistan.

title: Ruben Castillero Mortera
text: Ruben Castillero MORTERA, MSc AdvArc, is the Head of the Architecture Department at Paragon International University. He earned an MSc in Advanced Architectural Studies from the University of Strathclyde in the United Kingdom and a BA in Architecture from the National University of Mexico. He also holds a postgraduate diploma in Real Estate Management and Finance from the National Technological Autonomous Institute of Mexico. He has extensive academic and professional experience in architecture and interior design and has taught at universities in several countries. Professionally, he has worked as a design architect at various studios on the design, construction, and renovation of homes, offices, schools, hotels, and other projects. He has also worked as a model maker, creating architectural models for architectural companies, and as a freelance architect designing and supervising residential, hospitality, office, and warehouse projects. Education: MSc in Advanced Architectural Studies, University of Strathclyde, UK; BA in Architecture, National University of Mexico, Mexico.

title: Lida Sorn
text: Lida SORN, MSc CE, is the Head of the Civil Engineering Department and a lecturer at Paragon International University. He received his Master of Engineering in Civil Engineering from the Tokyo Institute of Technology in Japan in 2022. Before joining Paragon International University, he was a member of an Infrastructure Management Laboratory in the Department of Civil Engineering at Tokyo Tech. His research project was funded by Japan’s Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) in collaboration with Tokyo Tekko and Tokyo Tech and investigated the flexural behavior of precast concrete beams with connections using double grouted sleeves. He is also a member of Asia Japan Alumni (ASJA) International, which implements exchange programs for Japanese government MEXT scholarship students from ASEAN countries. Education: Master of Engineering in Civil Engineering, Tokyo Institute of Technology, Tokyo, Japan, 2022; BSc in Engineering, Zaman University, Phnom Penh, Cambodia, 2018.

title: Soriya Hoeur
text: Soriya HOEUR, M.Eng, is the Head of the Industrial Engineering Department at Paragon International University. He has academic, research, and industry experience spanning research, supply chain and logistics operations management, business statistics, strategy development, and project implementation. His research includes publications in Scopus-indexed journals focusing on performance measurement frameworks and modeling in industry. His professional experience also includes managing key accounts, leading aftersales departments, developing business strategies, conducting strategic analysis, and working with statistics initiatives. He earned a Master of Engineering in Industrial Engineering from Mahidol University, Thailand, in 2016. His academic interests include operational solution design, operation improvement, product and service development, technology acceptance models, and data science. Education: Master of Engineering in Industrial Engineering, Mahidol University, Thailand, 2016.

title: Pisith Hun
text: Pisith HUN, MSc, is a full-time lecturer at Paragon International University and a licensed architect with professional experience in architectural design and urban planning. He holds a Master of Urban and Regional Planning from The University of Queensland and a Bachelor’s degree in Architecture and Urbanism from the Royal University of Fine Arts. Since 2014, he has worked in professional roles including Architectural Design Manager, Design Consultant, and Architect, leading projects ranging from residential and corporate buildings to initiatives supporting informal settlement upgrading. Before joining Paragon International University as a full-time lecturer, he served as an adjunct lecturer at the Royal University of Fine Arts and Kirirom Institute of Technology. His teaching areas include architectural design studios, landscape architecture, sustainable design, and urban planning. He also participates in academic and professional initiatives as a panelist, judge, and mentor in international and local events. His research interests include architecture pedagogy, urban planning, informal settlement upgrading, gated communities, landscape architecture, and informal planning. Education: MSc in Urban and Regional Planning, The University of Queensland, Australia; BA in Architecture and Urbanism, Royal University of Fine Arts, Cambodia; BA in English for Professional Communication, Royal University of Phnom Penh, Cambodia.

title: Ranysakol Thuon
text: Ranysakol THUON, M.Eng, is a lecturer in the Civil Engineering Department at Paragon International University and is listed by the department as the Coordinator of the Civil Engineering Department. His areas of research interest and expertise include geotechnical engineering, building foundation design, soil mechanics, rock mechanics, engineering geology, deep excavation, and tunneling. Paragon International University also identifies his research areas as Geotechnical Engineering, Soil Mechanics, Rock Mechanics, Geological Engineering, and Tunneling.

title: Bradley Jensen Murg
text: Bradley Jensen MURG, Ph.D, is Professor, Provost, and Vice Rector for Academic Affairs at Paragon International University. He first visited Cambodia in 2000 as a Henry Luce Scholar working at the Asian Development Bank. He also holds appointments as Adjunct Research Fellow at Pacific Forum in Honolulu, Distinguished Research Fellow and Senior Advisor at the Cambodia Institute for Cooperation and Peace, co-editor of The Journal of Greater Mekong Studies, and Research Fellow at the Central European Institute for Asian Studies. His research focuses on contemporary international relations in Southeast Asia, the political economy of development, and comparative post-communism. Before joining Paragon International University full-time, he spent seven years as a professor and director of Global Development Studies at Seattle Pacific University and was an affiliate professor at the Henry M. Jackson School of International Affairs at the University of Washington. His research languages include English, French, Mandarin Chinese, Russian, and German. Education: Ph.D. in Political Science, University of Washington, USA, 2015; M.A. in Political Science, University of Washington, USA, 2008; MSc in Economic History, London School of Economics and Political Science, UK, 2002; M.A. in Philosophy, Emory University, USA, 2000; B.A. in Philosophy and International Affairs, Emory University, USA, 2000, Honors/Phi Beta Kappa. His publications include work on the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Mechanism and Listening to the Voices of the Khmer Rouge: Memory and Atrocity in Anlong Veng.

title: Bulat Akhmetkarimov
text: Bulat AKHMETKARIMOV, Ph.D, is the Rector and an Associate Professor at Paragon International University. He earned his bachelor's degree in Economics from Ege University in Turkey, a master's degree in Political Science from the University of Cincinnati in the United States, and a Ph.D. in International Affairs from the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies. His research focuses on the history of international relations, the role of religion in international affairs, and Russian foreign policy. He has previously taught and conducted research in Turkey, the United States, and Russia. Education: Ph.D. in International Affairs, Johns Hopkins University, USA, 2015; M.A. in Political Science, University of Cincinnati, USA, 2009; B.A. in Economics, Ege University, Turkey, 2006. His publications address topics including Muslim communities in Tatarstan, traditional Islam in Russia, state policies toward religion in post-Soviet Russia, religious parties in Russia, political identity in Tatarstan, demographics, and Turkish politics.

title: Socheata Kim
text: Socheata KIM, M.A, is the Head of the Business Administration Department at Paragon International University. She earned a B.A. in Business Administration, majoring in Management, from the National University of Management in 2003. She continued her studies at Ryukoku University in Kyoto, Japan, where she earned a research-based Master of Arts in Economics in 2010. Her graduate work focused on Economics and Education, including the correlation between educational achievement and economic behavior. She returned to Cambodia in 2010 and began a career in higher education, serving as a faculty member at institutions including the Royal University of Phnom Penh, National University of Management, and Paragon International University. At Paragon International University she teaches business courses including Principles of Management, Public Relations, Organizational Behavior, Business Essentials, Business Ethics, Economics and Asian Markets, International Business, and Research Methodology. She has also pursued advanced study in Clinical Counseling Psychology. Education: M.A. in Psychology (Advanced), Clinical Counseling, Royal University of Phnom Penh, Cambodia; M.A. in Economics, Ryukoku University, Kyoto, Japan, 2010; B.A. in Business Administration, National University of Management, Phnom Penh, Cambodia, 2003.

title: Sokmeng Soeun
text: Sokmeng SOEUN, M.A, is the Head of the International Trade and Logistics Department and a lecturer at Paragon International University in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. He earned a Master of Arts in Applied Economics specializing in International Trade from the University of International Business and Economics in Beijing, China. His fields of work and research interest include international trade theory and policy, monetary policy, human capital in development economics, and logistics operations. He teaches International Economics and Maritime Transportation Management to undergraduate students. Before entering academia, he gained professional experience in the shipping and logistics industry. Education: M.A. in Applied Economics, University of International Business and Economics, Beijing, China, 2017; B.A. in International Studies, Royal University of Phnom Penh, Cambodia, 2015; B.S. in Computer Science, National University of Management, Phnom Penh, Cambodia, 2014.

title: Marivic Cruz Gallego
text: Marivic CRUZ GALLEGO, M.A, is the Director of the Writing Center at Paragon International University. She is an experienced educator who has taught foreign nationals in regular and private schools since 2006. Her professional expertise includes staff development, teaching methodologies, higher education, educational technology, lesson planning, curriculum development, school event hosting, and lecturing. She joined Paragon International University in 2019 as a full-time lecturer in Academic English and Business courses and was appointed acting Director of the Writing Center in 2022. She earned her undergraduate degree in English from the University of the Cordilleras in the Philippines and a master's degree from Benguet State University. During more than ten years in China, she worked as a Programme Foundation Teacher, IELTS Trainer, and professor of Professional Communication and Business Communication. She also volunteered in English Corners at public schools to help students improve spoken English. Education: M.A. in Education, Benguet State University, La Trinidad, Philippines, 2007; B.S.Ed. in English, University of the Cordilleras, Baguio, Philippines, 2003.

title: Samnang Kong
text: Samnang KONG, B.A, is a Lecturer at Paragon International University. He earned a Bachelor of Sociology from the Royal University of Phnom Penh in 2011. Before joining Paragon International University as a full-time faculty member, he accumulated more than 12 years of professional business experience in Cambodia's corporate sector. His roles included Public Relations Manager at Huawei Cambodia, Business Development Manager at VisionFund Cambodia, and Marketing Manager at Chevrolet Cambodia. Alongside his corporate career, he taught undergraduate students at various universities and institutes in Phnom Penh. At Paragon International University, he is a lecturer in the Business Administration Department and teaches courses including Business Essentials, Retail Business, Public Relations, Organizational Behavior, and Human Resource Management. Education: Bachelor of Sociology, Royal University of Phnom Penh, Cambodia, 2011.

title: Phanny Ith
text: Phanny ITH, Ph.D, is the Head of the Banking and Finance Department and Assistant Professor at Paragon International University within the Faculty of Economics and Administrative Sciences. He has professional experience in academia as well as banks and financial institutions, including experience with a leading international commercial bank. His professional expertise includes actuarial analysis, product development and management, business performance and analytics, risk management, compliance, and digital project management. He has also contributed to partnerships between banking and financial institutions and the university and serves as a faculty advisor for the CFA Institute Research Challenge. His teaching and educational experience spans Khmer and English, mathematics, finance, banking, and accounting. His research interests include mathematics, finance, banking, financial inclusion, digital inclusion, leadership, and Teaching English as a Foreign Language. He is pursuing a Ph.D. in Management at Saint Louis University in the Philippines and holds graduate degrees in Mathematics and Finance and Banking as well as undergraduate degrees in Mathematics and TEFL. Education: Ph.D. in Management, in progress, Saint Louis University, Philippines; M.A. in Finance and Banking, National University of Management, Phnom Penh, Cambodia; MSc in Mathematics, Royal University of Phnom Penh, Cambodia; BSc in Mathematics, Royal University of Phnom Penh, Cambodia; BEd in TEFL, Western University, Phnom Penh, Cambodia.

title: Kashif Hasan Khan
text: Kashif Hasan Khan, PhD, is Professor of Economics and Finance, Dean of the School of Graduate Studies, and Head of the Department of Economics at Paragon International University. He specializes in international trade and geo-economics, particularly economic corridors and global financial architecture. He is the founder of the concept of Corridor Economics, a framework examining how connectivity infrastructure influences global trade patterns, geopolitical dynamics, and regional economic integration. His research also includes the Asymmetric Distance and Business Cycles framework, which examines asymmetric distance shocks in gravity-based trade models within a New Keynesian DSGE framework. His scholarly work has appeared in international journals including the Journal of Economic Integration, Journal of Economic Asymmetries, Maritime Economics & Logistics, Research in Globalization, Complexity, and India Quarterly. He has edited academic books on economic corridors and global connectivity and contributes policy commentary on global economic and geopolitical developments. He has held academic and corporate positions in Kyrgyzstan, Turkey, India, the Philippines, and the United Kingdom. He is an Editorial Board Member of the Asian Journal of Economic Modelling and Associate Editor of Crossroads of Social Inquiry at Abu Dhabi University. Education: Ph.D. in Economics, Jamia Millia Islamia University, New Delhi, India, 2009-2013; Certificate Course in Applied Data Science, Indian Institute of Technology Palakkad, India, 2022-2023.

title: Daniiar Satybaldiev
text: Dr Daniiar Satybaldiev earned his B.A. and M.Eng degrees in Industrial Electronics from International Ala-Too University, Kyrgyzstan, in 2009, and completed his PhD in Computer Science at Black Sea University, Georgia, in 2016. He served as a lecturer in Industrial Electronics at International Ala-Too University from 2009 to 2019. Since 2019, he has been a lecturer in the Computer Science Department at Paragon International University, Cambodia, teaching software engineering, programming, databases, cloud computing, and AI-related subjects. Alongside his academic role, he has held key leadership positions at the university, including Academic Affairs Coordinator and Director of the ERP and Web Development Office, where he leads digital transformation initiatives and ERP system innovations. His research focuses on artificial intelligence, ERP systems, embedded systems integration, and software development. He has presented his work at international conferences, receiving a “Best Paper Award” for a study on AI integration in educational ERP systems. He has also represented Cambodia at global events such as the Water in Transition Symposium in Hannover and serves as a program coordinator for international sustainability and AI workshops.

title: Sa Math
text: Dr. Sa Math earned his BS in Telecommunication and Electronic Engineering from the Royal University of Phnom Penh, Cambodia, in 2018, and completed his PhD in Software Convergence at Soonchunhyang University, Republic of Korea, in 2022, specializing in softwarization, virtual networking, and QoS/QoE engineering for next-generation mobile networks. His doctoral research focused on autonomous networking and resource management for SDN/NFV-based 6G TSN services. Since 2022, he has served as a Telecommunication Networking Specialist at the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications of Cambodia (MPTC), where he plays a key role in national digital infrastructure and connectivity initiatives, including 5G roadmap development, government network architecture, spectrum efficiency planning, and network security frameworks. He also contributes to major government projects related to digital services, next-generation mobile networking technologies, and 5G deployment for both public and industrial applications. In parallel, he is a senior R&D collaborator at the Mobile Computing and Networking Lab of Soonchunhyang University, working on AI-driven models for 5G/6G networks. His research spans next-generation mobile networking (NGMN), QoS/QoE, traffic engineering, O-RAN, network softwarization, virtualization, and edge computing. He has published more than 50 research articles in high-impact journals and conferences, including IEEE, Springer, MDPI, and Hindawi, and serves as a peer reviewer for several leading international ICT journals. Dr. Math has received multiple international research awards, including Best Paper Awards from APIC-IST, ICSMB, and Korea Internet Information conferences.

title: Alumni
text: The Alumni Affairs is administered under the Office of Student Services of Paragon International University.
